problem.explanation: Keep a `slow` pointer that indicates the position of the last unique element. Iterate through the array with a `fast` pointer. If `nums[fast] != nums[slow]`, increment `slow` and set `nums[slow] = nums[fast]`.
hints: Use a fast and slow pointer.
problem.statement_markdown: Given an integer array `nums` sorted in non-decreasing order, remove the duplicates in-place such that each unique element appears only once. The relative order of the elements should be kept the same. Return the first `k` unique elements as a list.
problem.title: Remove duplicates from sorted array
